instructions:
CatPaw is a headless browser. Navigate to a URL, read the snapshot that comes back, act on elements by their ref, read the result, repeat.

Snapshot lines: `e12 link "Sign in"` is an element (ref, role, name), followed by its state in brackets: [value=...], [checked], [disabled], [expanded]; [clickable] marks an element that looks clickable without a role. `text: ...` lines are page text. Indentation is nesting. The first line gives the snapshot id, tab, document, URL and title, and settled=no when the page was still busy.

After an action you get what changed since the last snapshot: `~` changed, `+` added (new refs are usable at once), `-` removed, `>` moved; `(replaces e13)` means the page re-rendered that element under a new ref. A new document comes back whole. Pass snapshot:"full" for the whole page.

Refs: an element keeps its ref across snapshots until it leaves the page, and refs are never reused. A ref that went stale gives `error StaleRef` naming the likely replacement. Prefer refs; use css:<selector> for elements no snapshot shows and xy:<x>,<y> as a last resort.

Results start with `ok`, `error <Code>` (nothing happened; the message says why and what to try), `needs_confirmation` (the user must approve; follow the message) or `blocked` (not allowed; do not retry). Lines starting with `!` report consequences: navigations, new tabs, dialogs, requests, console errors, and what kept the page busy.

type replaces a field's value unless append is true. Dialogs are dismissed unless the action says dialog:"accept" (promptText answers a prompt). Windows a page opens become tabs. When something is still loading, wait for it. To read content rather than act on it, use read; logs shows console messages and requests. Screenshots cost many tokens; take them when layout or images matter.

tools.description:
Open a URL in the current tab (opening a tab when there is none), or go back, forward or reload. Returns the page's snapshot.
Example: {"url":"https://example.com"}

go.description: A history move instead of a URL

url.description: https:// is assumed when no scheme is given

tools.name: navigate
tools.title: Navigate

tools.description:
Show the current tab as a tree: one line per element worth reading or acting on, each with a ref (e12) that other tools take as target. Actions already return what changed; call this to see the whole page again, with another filter, or one part of it.
Example: {"filter":"interactive"}

attrs.description: Extra attributes: link URLs, image sources, descriptions

diff.description: Only what changed since the last snapshot

filter.description: interesting (default): controls, headings, landmarks and text; interactive: controls only; all: every element

format.description: compact (default): e12 link "Home"; aria: - link "Home" [ref=e12]. Later results use it too

root.description: Ref of a subtree to show alone

tools.name: snapshot
tools.title: Snapshot

tools.description:
Click an element: scroll it into view, check that nothing covers it, click its centre. Returns the outcome and what changed on the page.
Example: {"target":"e12"}
tools.name: click
tools.title: Click

tools.description:
Type into a text field or editable element, replacing its value unless append is true; submit presses Enter afterwards. Without target, types into the focused element.
Example: {"target":"e5","text":"catpaw","submit":true}

append.description: Keep the current value and add to it

tools.name: type
tools.title: Type

tools.description:
Press a key or chord on the focused element, or on target after focusing it: Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown, Backspace, Control+a, Shift+Tab.
Example: {"key":"Enter"}
tools.name: press
tools.title: Press key

tools.description:
Choose an option of a <select> by its visible label (or value); an array chooses several in a multiple select. When nothing matches, the error lists the options.
Example: {"target":"e8","option":"Price (low to high)"}
tools.name: select
tools.title: Select option

tools.description:
Less common element actions: hover, check, uncheck, focus, clear (empty a field), scroll (target into view, or the page by dy pixels; one screen down by default).
Example: {"kind":"check","target":"e14"}

dy.description: Page scroll in pixels; negative scrolls up

tools.name: act
tools.title: Other action

tools.description:
Read the current tab as text rather than a tree. markdown: the content, links as [text](ref:e12); text: plain text; links: ref, text and URL per line; forms: fields with refs, values and options; tables: Markdown tables with row refs; find: where query (text or /regex/) occurs, with refs; html: the markup. Long output stops at maxTokens and says which offset continues it.
Example: {"view":"markdown"}

main.description: markdown and text: only the main content, when the page marks it

root.description: Ref of the part to read

tools.name: read
tools.title: Read

tools.description:
A PNG of the current tab's viewport, or of the whole page. Costs far more tokens than a snapshot; take one when layout, images or canvas matter.
Example: {}
tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot

tools.description:
Run JavaScript in the page and return the result as a console shows it; promises are awaited. The script is an expression, or statements that return. el is the target's element; $ref("e12") gives any ref's element.
Example: {"script":"el.value","target":"e5"}
tools.name: evaluate
tools.title: Evaluate JavaScript

tools.description:
List, switch to, open or close tabs. A window a page opens becomes a tab, and the action that opened it names it.
Example: {"op":"switch","tab":"t2"}

tab.description: Tab id; close defaults to the current tab

tools.name: tabs
tools.title: Tabs

tools.description:
Let the page run until it settles, a text appears or goes, an element is visible, the URL contains a string, or ms milliseconds pass. Time the page spends only waiting on timers passes at once. Returns what changed.
Example: {"for":"text","text":"Order placed"}

target.description: For visible and gone: ref or css:<selector>

url.description: For url: part of the URL

tools.name: wait
tools.title: Wait

tools.description:
The current tab's console messages, requests, or events (navigations, new tabs, dialogs), oldest first.
Example: {"kind":"console","level":"error"}
tools.name: logs
tools.title: Logs
